exposure: pattern compatible with retained products of conception (RPOC) in transvaginal ultrasonography
fever during the first 14 days after delivery
Patients with and without the need for curettage
finding: Endometritis was the main cause of puerperal fever (52.7%), and factors associated with the need for curettage included the presence of retained products of conception on ultrasound, fever in the first 14 days postpartum, abdominal pain, and malodorous lochia, while scheduled cesarean delivery was protective.
mod_finding: Scheduled cesarean delivery was protective against the need for curettage (OR: 0.11 [95% CI 0.01-1.2]; P-value 0.08).
